purpose: This tool shows four ways to write the same stretch of numbers: a list, a rule, a graph and interval brackets. You test numbers against a rule, build intervals, and combine two sets with and or or.

stops.title: What the figure shows
stops.text: Step 1 shows number tokens 0 to 7. Tap one to put it in the set or take it out. Steps 2 to 4 show a number line. In step 2, drag the test point along the line. Green means in the set and red means out.
stops.try: In step 1, tap a number on the figure and watch the set in braces change.

stops.title: Test a number
stops.text: Step 1. This slider picks a number n, and the readout says if n is in the set or not. The number buttons add or remove numbers. Write it another way shows the same set in other forms. Empty the set clears it.
stops.try: Test n = 5, then press 5 in the row to add it and test again.

stops.title: Test point and the rule
stops.text: Step 2. The four buttons above pick a rule such as x at least 2 or x greater than 2. Drag the point on the number line or use this slider, and the readout says in or out. Show the whole set draws the full set.
stops.try: Test x = 2 with greater than or equal, then switch to greater than.

stops.title: Build or read
stops.text: Step 3. Answer the prediction first, then the steppers and bracket buttons unlock. Build an interval makes brackets from a graph rule. Read a graph does the reverse: you read a graph and give the notation.
stops.try: Predict, then build (-1, 4] with the steppers and bracket buttons.

stops.title: Square and round brackets
stops.text: Step 3. A square bracket means the end number is included (closed circle). A round bracket means it is not (open circle). Infinity always gets a round bracket, because you can never reach it.
stops.try: Make the left end not included and watch the circle open.

stops.title: And, or
stops.text: Step 4. Pick a case with two rules, such as x greater than -2 and x at most 3. Press and for the overlap, or for everything in either set. The combined set appears in violet. Then pick its notation.
stops.try: Pick case C and try both and and or.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 builds sets of numbers. Step 2 describes a set with a rule. Step 3 writes intervals with brackets. Step 4 combines sets with and, or, and looks at the inputs of 1/x.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Three questions at the end. A wrong answer explains why.

teacher: Project step 3 and have students predict which end of -1 < x <= 4 is closed. Common mistakes: using a square bracket next to infinity, and mixing up 'and' with 'or' in step 4. Ask: why can 2 be in a set for x >= 2 but not for x > 2?
